events.title: A rover mission reaches Mars
events.description: Pathfinder lands carrying the small Sojourner rover.

events.title: The euro begins
events.description: Eleven countries start sharing a currency for financial transactions. Euro notes and coins will arrive later.

events.title: The September 11 attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks kill thousands of people in the United States. Families, communities and rescuers face devastating losses.

what_happened_next.text:
By September 2001, one dollar in Microsoft had become about $3.10, and one dollar in Apple about $1.40. Nike ended at roughly 79 cents. The U.S. share basket gained overall, but Apple had a steep fall along the way. Comparing only the endpoints misses the difficult middle and can make later winners look obvious when they were not.

Company news was mixed. Nike’s fiscal-1998 revenue rose 4% to $9.6 billion, but net income fell almost half as demand weakened and extra inventory needed discounts. Apple said it had shipped five million iMacs by April 2001. Microsoft reported $25.3 billion in fiscal-2001 revenue, 10% above the year before. These facts describe their businesses, not a simple cause for each stock’s five-year result.

Pathfinder reached Mars and the euro began for financial transactions during these years. The September 11 attacks came in the final month and caused devastating losses to people and communities. The chart cannot show that human impact. The window ends in September 2001, so later events cannot be used to explain its ending values. A broad basket can reduce one company’s effect without removing risk.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Investors compared famous fund managers with indexes. Computer competition, an internet attack and Tiger Woods’s professional debut also drew attention.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The route to the final value mattered. A positive five-year total could include losses that would have been hard to sit through.
reflection.what_faded_away: An athlete’s promising career did not guarantee a rising sponsor’s share price. The most popular investment manager was not automatically the best choice either.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The exact technology-stock reversals and the September 11 attacks were unknown. No confident starting story removed those risks.

hot:1996-09:nike.text: Nike’s fiscal 1998 revenue rose 4% to a record $9.6 billion, but net income fell nearly half to $399.6 million. Weak demand and extra inventory led to discounting, squeezing profit even as sales reached a record.

hot:1996-09:apple.text: On April 19, 2001, Apple announced it had shipped its five millionth iMac. Its all-in-one design helped attract buyers looking for a colorful, simpler Mac, adding sales during a difficult stretch for the company.

hot:1996-09:microsoft.text: Microsoft reported fiscal-year revenue of $25.30 billion on July 19, 2001, up 10% from a year earlier. Windows and software for work and home were still selling well, showing demand remained strong across the company’s core business.
